title: Ethiopian Cinnamon Milk
community: Ethiopian households — the bedtime sweet milk
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Warm Milk — whole milk warmed with cinnamon, cardamom, and a generous spoonful of Ethiopian honey. The bedtime drink that Ethiopian parents make for children and the comfort drink for adults on cold highland evenings.
longDesc: Ethiopian spiced warm milk is the bedtime ritual of Ethiopian households — the highland evenings are cold, and a warm cup of honey-cinnamon milk is the most comforting ending to the day.
steps: Warm milk with cinnamon stick and cardamom pods over medium-low heat.
Bring to just below boiling — steaming but not boiling.
chefTips: Never boil milk — scalds and produces a skin.
Add honey off the heat — preserves enzyme activity.
commonMistakes: Adding honey to very hot milk.
cookingScience: Cinnamon's cinnamaldehyde dissolves into warm milk fat — distributing the aroma and flavour uniformly. The honey's glucose oxidase (enzyme) is denatured above 40°C — adding it to very hot milk destroys its antimicrobial activity.
culturalNote: Ethiopian spiced warm milk is the language of parental care — the cup brought to a child on a cold evening, the drink prepared for an elderly parent, the self-care ritual of adults who know how to be gentle with themselves. It is warmth in liquid form.
